structured_output.world_model:
W1 (mechanism), after E025. Tip E023: 225 steps (9.0 true epochs, 25 steps/epoch at batch 2000), 24/28/32 px at 40/30/30%, Muon on renormalized filters, Lookahead alpha exponent 3, 6.198 s, 0.7538; its true mean is probably about 0.7535. E025 (alpha exponent 2) gave 0.7557 at the same time and was discarded. That fits my prior that averaging-strength and regularization knobs sit within ±0.2 pp, so I038 was not kept, and I042 takes branch (b).

**Time model.** Time follows pixel-steps almost 1:1. Pixel-weighted time shares: 24 px about 30%, 28 px 30%, 32 px 40%. The last 25% of steps is about 33% of train time.

**Conv MAC shares.** Group 1 is about 20% of conv MACs (31² conv1, 15² conv2/3), group 2 about 51%, group 3 about 29%. Skipping group-1 backward saves about 13–15% of a tail step.

**Batch.** Raising batch at fixed epochs saves only fixed per-step costs: the Muon Newton-Schulz step, the optimizer and Lookahead launches, and CUDA-graph replay. That is roughly 3–6%.

**Accuracy.** Fewer steps or epochs cost about 0.25 pp per 10% of time. Muon lr and wd sit on a flat optimum. Loss-based filtering at LS 0.3 with stale losses from other resolutions is roughly equal to an epoch cut, so it adds no gain. The current margin is about 0.05–0.15 pp, so most trims below 9 epochs are coin flips at 3 seeds.

forecasts.reason: Branch (b) goes from 225 to 219 steps: −2.7% pixel-steps gives about −0.16 s and about −0.07 pp, well inside the ±0.3 pp RNG reshuffle, so whether it lands feasible is a coin flip.

The truncated tail is about 1.9 s of train time; dropping group-1 wgrad and dgrad (about 20% of MACs × 2/3) saves about 0.25 s. Annealing group 1 to 0 early costs about 0.1–0.2 pp, and the 4% bar is borderline.
About −9% steps gives about −0.45 s. Losses come from mixed resolutions and are smoothed by LS 0.3, so selection acts like an epoch cut (about −0.25 pp) and likely misses 0.753.

Same pixels with 20% fewer steps saves only per-step fixed cost (Newton-Schulz, optimizer, Lookahead), about 4%. The 20% fewer Muon updates cost about 0.2–0.3 pp, so it is borderline against the 0.15 pp bar.
With renormalized filters, lr sets the angular step size. ×1.5 was flat; ×2 is likely past the optimum and gives a flat-to-slightly-negative result, not +0.2 pp.

cruxes: What is E023's held-out seeds 3–12 mean? If it is at or below 0.753, every trim below 9 epochs is infeasible, and the loop should look for a real booster instead.
What fraction of a 32 px step is per-step fixed cost (Newton-Schulz, optimizer, Lookahead, graph launch) rather than conv compute? This sets whether batch 2500 saves 2% or 8%.
Does freezing group 1 for the last 25% of steps cost less accuracy than an equal-time epoch cut? That is, does group 1 actually change little late in training under Muon's fixed-norm updates?
